**Amakashinimasu Shrine** (あまかしにますじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located on {{ill|Amakashi-no-Oka|Q11574286|qid=Q11574286}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|Q752397|qid=Q752397}}, {{ill|Takaichi District, Nara|Q1117901|qid=Q1117901}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288|qid=Q134917288}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
{{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} is enshrined as the principal deity. The subsidiary shrines enshrine {{ill|Hachiman shrine|Q11390939|qid=Q11390939}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kasuga Daimyōjin}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|Q11568925|qid=Q11568925}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sumiyoshi Daimyōjin}}, and {{ill|Kumano Gongen|Q11568925|qid=Q11568925}}. According to the *Gogun Jinja-ki*, the deities were {{ill|Magatsuhi-no-kami|Q11591203|qid=Q11591203|lt=Yasomagatsuhinokami and Ōmagatsuhinokami}} and {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|Q11581794|qid=Q11581794|lt=Kamunaobi no Kami and Ōnaobi no Kami}}, which are believed to have been the original enshrined deities. Empress Suiko came to be worshipped as the principal deity only from the Edo period onward.

=== History ===
The shrine is said to have been founded by {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}. An entry dated the 27th day of the first month of Jōgan 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}} records that Amakashi no Kami was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade. The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} lists it as “Amakashinimasu Shrine, four seats, Takaichi District, {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}},” classifying it as a major shrine and noting that it received offerings at the Tsukinami, Ainame, and Niiname festivals.

=== Rituals ===
[[File:Amakashinimasu-jinja2.jpg|thumb|250px|Amakashinimasu Shrine (Kugatachi)]]
Amakashi Hill was, in ancient times, a place where {{ill|Kuchiyose|Q11581453|qid=Q11581453}} (ordeal by boiling water) was performed, and medieval sources such as the *Gogun Jinja-ki* describe this shrine as a “deity of hot-water divination.” In connection with this tradition, the Kugatachi ritual has been performed at the shrine since the postwar period.<ref>[http://www.bell.jp/pancho/kasihara_diary/2003_04_06.htm Viewing the Kugatachi ritual at Amakashinimasu Shrine]</ref><ref>[https://asukamura.com/experience/549/ Kugatachi]</ref>
